name: Cellular Base-Station Ingest Nodes
description: The INGEST half of the cellular program. cell-tower-source is the REQUEST-scoped browser aggregate - one $HTQ in, one deconflicted $TBS stream straight back to the caller, capabilities [], nothing persisted. That is the right shape for the demo and the wrong shape for ingest, and the two cannot be one flow, so the ingest-only decisions live here, exactly as the credential lane was split into cell-tower-credentials for the same reason. This plugin REUSES cell-tower-source's parse and deconflict unchanged: decoding a provider body and merging sites across providers are the same operations whether the answer is served or stored, and forking them would fork the deconfliction rules. Four pure nodes plan a ranged chunk against a durable resume mark, author the storage attribution, and advance the mark only on a verified store. NO CAPABILITIES: http, storage and flatsql are the generic hostcap connector nodes, so this plugin performs no I/O and needs no new host connector.

sequentialJustification.detail: All four methods are single-pass transforms over the frames the flow hands them: they format a query, a fetch descriptor, an attribution frame or a mark. There is no shared mutable state, no worker pool and no fan-out inside the guest. This guest can never spawn a thread, so it compiles clang/wasi-sequential rather than claiming a wasi-threads contract it does not honour.

methods.description: THE CACHE GATE (owner 2026-08-14: 'the cell towers should load almost instantaneously'). Sits between the flow's one http trigger and cell-tower-source's route. An /aggregate read is answered FROM THE STORE - one FlatSQL SELECT over rows the cellular-network-ingest timer already persisted, streamed back verbatim by hostcap/flatsql-query - instead of fanning out a live GET per provider and merging the bodies while the caller waits (~9s on the live page). Every other route, and any request carrying REFRESH:true, is passed through to route UNCHANGED, so the live provider lane stays intact and reachable; it is simply no longer the default. Provider refresh belongs to the timer flow, never the request path. Emits on exactly ONE lane per request, so two bodies can never race into respond. The SQL is node CONFIG (cell_cache_sql), not a compiled-in constant - this is the first concrete instance of the per-dataset DEFAULT QUERY contract (graph task sdn-dataset-default-query-materialized-cache). A request whose envelope cannot be read is FORWARDED, never answered from cache: serving the last good answer to a request nobody could parse is the one failure this gate must not introduce. NO NEW HOST SURFACE - plugin.getConfig plus flatsql-query frames over existing generic hooks; the plugin stays capabilities []. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). A surplus is refused with error code "batched-input-frames", naming the port and the count.

methods.description: THE HONEST HALF OF THE CACHE. A cache that answers instantly and says nothing about its age is worse than the fetch it replaced, because a stale answer becomes indistinguishable from a current one. This node authors the decision envelope that rides beside the cached record stream so the UI can say WHEN the towers it is drawing were ingested. It reports only what it can establish: cacheState 'empty' when the ingest lane has left no mark (instant AND empty, with the reason named and REFRESH:true offered as the direct route to the providers - the task's 'no fake instant-but-empty answers'); cacheState 'warm' with the provider and byte progress the mark carries; and freshness 'unavailable' when a mark frame is present but not readable as the JSON ingest_plan already expects on this port, because the mark read lane is not yet closed end-to-end and a timestamp guessed at here would be a lie with a number on it. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). methods.description: Emits ONE ranged fetch descriptor plus the cell-tower-source run contract for that chunk. The chunk size is clamped to 4 MiB because the Go server host caps an http response body there (hostcap/http-request manifest): a larger ask is TRUNCATED by the host and parses to a plausible short row set with no error anywhere. One chunk per tick rather than an in-guest loop, so the loop's state lives in the durable mark instead of in a guest instance a restart erases. Emits nothing once the mark shows the object complete, and fails closed when no cell_ingest_url is configured. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). methods.description: Authors the attribution the storage lane cannot invent (provider, source, batch, $TBS.SOURCES provenance) and forwards the records untouched. Takes the http response because the object's TOTAL SIZE is only knowable from Content-Range's denominator - Content-Length on a 206 describes the chunk, and reading it as the total would end the run after one chunk with every later byte silently unfetched. Uses reconcile=append, NOT the source-batch reconcile the celestrak lane uses: this batch is one CHUNK of the provider's set, not the set, and reconciling would delete every earlier chunk as the next arrived. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider). methods.description: Advances the resume mark from the STORAGE RESULT, never at dispatch: a mark advanced when a chunk is requested turns a crash between fetch and store into permanently skipped rows, invisibly. Catches the silent nop that survives hostcap/storage-ingest's own ok:false check - ok:true with inserted=0 for a chunk that carried records, which is byte-identical to a healthy empty tail - and refuses to advance the mark over rows that were never stored. The mark is NOT gated on the publish URL (a node that stores without publishing must still make progress); publication itself is fail-closed, emitting nothing when unconfigured. BATCHING: every input port here is single-stream BY CONTRACT and that is ENFORCED IN CODE. maxStreams/maxBatch/drainPolicy are purely DECLARATIVE in the compiled flow runtime, which drains a node's queue port-blind up to a budget of 64, so a node that read ordinal 0 and returned used to destroy every other frame it was handed (live P1 cellular-multiprovider-returns-only-first-provider).
